items.answer: Daiyu sneered, "I knew it. Unless the others have turned them down, I'm never given anything."

items.text: 賈母道：「讀的是什麼書，不過是認得兩個字，不是睜眼的瞎子罷了！」
items.answer: "What books are they reading?" said Grandmother Jia. "They've only learned to recognize a few characters. They're not blind, at least."

errors.evidence: "What books are they reading?" said Grandmother Jia.
errors.why: This renders the dismissive rhetorical question as a plain question, though the following sentences make clear she is downplaying their studies; the sense is partly kept.

errors.evidence: They're not blind, at least.
errors.why: The figure of 睜眼的瞎子 (a person with open eyes who is still blind, i.e. illiterate) is reduced to literal 'not blind', losing the illiteracy point, though the minimizing tone survives.

items.text: 賈母道：「讀的是什麼書，不過是認得兩個字，不是睜眼的瞎子罷了！」
items.answer: "What books are they reading?" said Grandmother Jia. "They only know a couple of characters, that's all. At least they're not blind!"

errors.evidence: "What books are they reading?" said Grandmother Jia.
errors.why: The dismissive rhetorical question is rendered as a plain question, though it is still plausibly read as rhetorical.

errors.evidence: At least they're not blind!
errors.why: The idiom 睜眼的瞎子 means illiterate, someone who can see but cannot read. 'Not blind' loses that and sounds like a literal comment on eyesight.

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」
items.answer: Fengjie said, "I've been telling you all day long that you're far too soft. If you let the household get away with this, where will it end?"

errors.evidence: I've been telling you all day long
errors.why: 成日家 means 'constantly/always', so the sentence is a habitual complaint; 'I've been telling you all day long' suggests one stretch of time today.

errors.evidence: let the household get away with this
errors.why: 家裡人 means the household's servants or retainers, not the household as a whole; this is a small loss of precision.

items.text: 鳳姐道：「我成日家說你太軟弱了，縱的家裡人這樣還了得了。」
items.answer: Feng Jie said, "I've been telling you all day long that you're too soft. Letting the household people get away with this sort of thing—how could it ever be tolerated?"

errors.evidence: Feng Jie said
errors.why: 鳳姐 is Xifeng (Wang Xifeng); "Feng Jie" is a non-standard rendering of the nickname, though still recognizable.

errors.evidence: I've been telling you all day long
errors.why: 成日家 means constantly; "all day long" is acceptable, but the present perfect progressive slightly changes the habitual sense.

errors.evidence: the household people
errors.why: "household people" is awkward; "servants" or "household staff" would be more natural and clearer.

errors.evidence: I've been telling you all day
errors.why: 成日家 means constantly or always, not literally 'all day' on this occasion; the sense is that she says it habitually.

errors.evidence: Feng Jie

errors.evidence: the household people

items.text: 你生氣，要打罵人容易，何苦摔那命根子！
items.answer: "You're angry, and it's easy enough to strike or scold someone. Why throw down your very lifeline like that?"

items.text: 你生氣，要打罵人容易，何苦摔那命根子！
items.answer: "You're angry, and it's easy enough to strike out and scold someone. Why must you smash that treasure of yours?"

errors.evidence: Why must you smash that treasure of yours?
errors.why: 命根子 means 'life-root', his very lifeline; 'treasure' is a weaker rendering that loses the sense of what he cannot live without, though it still points at the jade.

items.text: 你生氣，要打罵人容易，何苦摔那命根子！
items.answer: "You're in a temper, and it's easy enough to strike or scold someone. Why bother throwing away your life's treasure?"

errors.evidence: Why bother throwing away your life's treasure?
errors.why: 摔 means to smash or hurl down hard, and "throwing away" is weaker. "Life's treasure" also loses the 'life-root/lifeline' sense, though the gist of something most precious is kept.

items.text: 劉姥姥陪笑道：「我找太太的陪房周大爺的，煩那位太爺替我請他老出來。」

errors.why: 陪房 is a servant who came with the lady as part of her dowry; "attendant" loses the dowry-servant sense and the marriage link, though the gist is kept.

errors.evidence: Liu Laolao smiled and said

items.answer: Li Gui laughed and said, "Don't be angry with me, sir, but you have never really been proper in your ways, and that is why these young fellows won't listen to you."

items.answer: Li Gui laughed and said, "Don't blame me for speaking plainly, young master, but you have never been entirely proper in your ordinary conduct, and that is why these young fellows won't listen to you."

items.text: 李貴笑道：“不怕你老人家惱我，素日你老人家到底有些不正經，所以這些兄弟才不聽。

items.text: 臺磯之上，坐著幾個穿紅著綠的丫頭，一見他們來了，便忙都笑迎上來，說：「剛纔老太太還念呢，可巧就來了。」

items.answer: On the terrace steps sat several maids in red and green. The moment they saw the party coming, they hurried down to greet them with smiles and said, "The old lady was just speaking of you a moment ago, and you've come at just the right time."

errors.evidence: they hurried down to greet them
errors.why: The source says 忙都笑迎上來, meaning they hurried forward to meet them; "down" is not in the source and slightly shifts the direction.

errors.evidence: The old lady was just speaking of you
errors.why: Lowercase "old lady" can read as a generic old woman rather than the family matriarch, though context makes it understandable.

items.text: 作者自云：因曾歷過一番夢幻之後，故將真事隱去，而借通靈之說，撰此《石頭記》一書也。
items.answer: The author says of himself: having gone through a period like a dream, he hid the true events and borrowed the tale of the spirit-stone to write this book, *The Story of the Stone*.

items.text: 作者自云：因曾歷過一番夢幻之後，故將真事隱去，而借通靈之說，撰此《石頭記》一書也。
items.answer: The author says: having gone through a dream-like span of life, I have therefore hidden the true events and, borrowing the tale of the spirit-stone, written this book, *The Story of the Stone*.

errors.evidence: The author says: having gone through a dream-like span of life, I have therefore hidden
errors.why: The sentence shifts from third person ("The author says") to first person ("I"), and the participle "having gone" then dangles; the Chinese has no "I".

errors.evidence: a dream-like span of life
errors.why: 一番夢幻 means a spell or experience of dream and illusion, not a span of life; the rendering adds a nuance of lifespan.

items.text: 作者自云：因曾歷過一番夢幻之後，故將真事隱去，而借通靈之說，撰此《石頭記》一書也。
items.answer: The author says: having gone through a dream-like stretch of life, I have hidden the true events and borrowed the tale of a spirit-stone to write this book, The Story of the Stone.

errors.evidence: The author says: having gone through a dream-like stretch of life, I have hidden
errors.why: The sentence shifts from third person ("The author says") to first person ("I"), which is inconsistent. The source has no explicit pronoun and the key keeps third person.

errors.evidence: borrowed the tale of a spirit-stone
errors.why: 通靈 refers to the magic jade that can communicate spiritually, and "spirit-stone" is vague. The sense is close, so the meaning is mostly intact.

items.text: 祖師聞言，咄的一聲，跳下高臺，手持戒尺，指定悟空道：「你這猢猻，這般不學，那般不學，卻待怎麼？」

items.text: 祖師聞言，咄的一聲，跳下高臺，手持戒尺，指定悟空道：「你這猢猻，這般不學，那般不學，卻待怎麼？」
items.answer: When the Patriarch heard this, he gave a sharp "Tut!" and leapt down from the high platform. Holding a teacher's ruler, he pointed it at Wukong and said, "You little monkey, you won't study this and you won't study that. What do you expect to happen?"

errors.evidence: What do you expect to happen?
errors.why: 卻待怎麼 means "what do you want / what are you going to do"; "expect to happen" shifts the sense slightly but keeps the rebuking tone.

errors.evidence: Holding a teacher's ruler, he pointed it at Wukong
errors.why: 戒尺 is a disciplinary ruler or rod, which "teacher's ruler" blurs; "pointed it at" is acceptable for 指定.

items.text: 祖師聞言，咄的一聲，跳下高臺，手持戒尺，指定悟空道：「你這猢猻，這般不學，那般不學，卻待怎麼？」
items.answer: Hearing this, the Patriarch said "Tut!" and leapt down from the high platform. Holding a teacher's ruler, he pointed at Wukong and said, "You little monkey, you won't learn this and you won't learn that. What do you want, then?"

items.text: 有一般天罡數，該三十六般變化；有一般地煞數，該七十二般變化。

items.text: 這猴王也是他一竅通時百竅通，當時習了口訣，自修自煉，將七十二般變化都學成了。

items.text: 這猴王也是他一竅通時百竅通，當時習了口訣，自修自煉，將七十二般變化都學成了。

items.text: 這猴王也是他一竅通時百竅通，當時習了口訣，自修自煉，將七十二般變化都學成了。
items.answer: This monkey king, too, was one who, once one orifice was opened, had all the others opened as well; he learned the oral formula on the spot, practiced and refined it on his own, and mastered all seventy-two transformations.

items.text: 悟空道：「我自聞道之後，有七十二般地煞變化之功，觔斗雲有莫大的神通；善能隱身遯身，起法攝法。

errors.evidence: summoning and subduing by magic
errors.why: 起法攝法 means raising and drawing in/controlling magic, not 'subduing', which is a slight shift in sense.

items.text: 悟空道：「我自聞道之後，有七十二般地煞變化之功，觔斗雲有莫大的神通；善能隱身遯身，起法攝法。
